title: The legacy criterion of RWB-E4-049 is generic, its test cases carry no data and the story master gives no requirement id
source: Legacy RWB-E4-049 (Story, Acceptance criteria, Data, Test cases); FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.10.4.1 (AC-P8-010-01); work package line for RWB-P8-E4049-APP (reqs empty)
description: The story owns two legacy criteria word for word and both are generic. AC1 reads Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place / When its trigger arrives / Then applies every receipt to the balance in the order the policy sets / Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version, and AC2 reads Given the decision log cannot be written / When the action is taken / Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003. The four legacy test cases repeat the same rows with no receipt, amount, case or business date. The FSD keeps the feature as FEAT-PAY-10 and its main success criterion AC-P8-010-01 is one line marked Written one epic ahead, so the module document adds no value either. The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice, which is why section 18 of the app story traces the two criteria to FEAT-PAY-10 and AC-P8-010-01 rather than to a requirement row. The story therefore keeps the two criteria unchanged and supplies its own synthetic data set, which is where the receipt and the balance come from.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-049 AC1 and AC2 as quoted; legacy test cases TC-E4-049-01 Apply proceeds to the case balance and TC-E4-049-02 Not recorded with no data column; FSD P8 v3 A2.10.4.1 AC-P8-010-01 The data and rules it needs are in place / The trigger arrives / The result is recorded with its rule version / Written one epic ahead; the FSD Requirements served table of P8 is empty.
owner_role: P8 business analyst and the FSD owner
proposed: Have the P8 business analyst confirm the receipt and balance data set the E4 build tests on (case RC-2026-000555 with receipt PR-2026-000555 of source CUSTOMER for 12,500.00 THB on the business date) and carry it into the Story test cases tab of the Test Cases master under the same four test case IDs; add the requirement row of FEAT-PAY-10 to the Requirements served table of FSD P8 in its next version.

title: The application order of the proceeds is published nowhere, and the package code, the rule IDs, the applied state value and the run and activity names are not published either
source: Legacy RWB-E4-049 (Story, Acceptance criteria); FSD P8 v3 A2.10.1, A2.10.2 and A2.10.4.4; TSD P8 v2 T3.0, T3.1 and T3.2 (payment_match_rule, DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273); context pack P8 ownership rows
description: The legacy criterion requires the Workbench to apply every receipt to the balance in the order the policy sets, but no source publishes that order, its components, its percentages, its caps or the value the applied row takes in the state column of TSD P8 T3.0. The FSD describes the step only as receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer and applies the rules, and the TSD names payment_match_rule with match_type, amount_tolerance_pct, window_days_before, window_days_after, grace_days, partial_floor_pct and priority as columns while publishing no row value. No source gives the package code or the rule IDs of the application either, and no source names the JOB-07 run or its application activity. The story therefore holds every one of those values as a rule row, a reference-data value, a DB story enum or a placeholder, and names no invented rule, order, percentage or activity.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-049 AC1 Then applies every receipt to the balance in the order the policy sets; FSD P8 v3 A2.10.2 step 1 Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer and step 2 Applies the rules; TSD P8 v2 T3.0 lists state varchar(40) Record lifecycle state with no value; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 lists payment_match_rule with DF-REF-264 to DF-REF-270 and publishes no row value; the context pack lists no package code and no workflow name for this service.
owner_role: P7 rule owner and the P8 solution architect
proposed: Publish the application order of the PAYMENT_MATCH package as rule rows with their components, sequence and caps and their package code and rule IDs in the rule registry, name the applied state value in the physical schema of rwb_payment, and name the JOB-07 run and its application activity in the Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog; the story then replaces the placeholders and changes no criterion.

title: The legacy story reads v_ace_account and v_ace_payment in process while the target gives the ACE views to rwb-source-data alone
source: Legacy RWB-E4-049 (Data, Endpoints); FSD P8 v3 change note and A2.10.3.1 (VR-P8-010-1); context pack P8 (no ACE grant) and the slide 8 note on the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-05
description: The legacy Data table lists v_ace_account with DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042 and v_ace_payment with DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054 as sources of the application, and VR-P8-010-1 reads v_ace_batch_status for the staleness check, all in process. In the target only rwb-source-data holds SELECT on the recovery.v_ace_* views and every other service holds no grant, so DP-05 applies to this service as a prohibition and not as a permission: the receipts, the account balance and the batch status arrive on the rwb-source-data contract. The story keeps the staleness rule and its message exactly and moves the read, and the difference between the legacy data table and the target grant is recorded here so that the FSD data table and the DP-05 row agree in their next versions.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-049 Data rows v_ace_account DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042 and v_ace_payment DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054; FSD P8 v3 A2.10.3.1 VR-P8-010-1 reads v_ace_batch_status; the context pack describes the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views as read only by rwb-source-data and lists no ACE table among the P8 ownership rows; Architecture v5 slide 29 gives the views to rwb-source-data.
owner_role: P1 source-data owner and the P8 solution architect
proposed: Keep the receipt, balance and batch-status reads on the rwb-source-data contract with its freshness stamp, retire the v_ace_account, v_ace_payment and v_ace_batch_status reads of this service, and correct the Data table of FSD P8 and the DP-05 row of the pattern table so that no service but rwb-source-data is drawn as an ACE view reader.

title: The applied-amount answer, the MatchRequest field list, the ProceedsMatched payload and the rwb-case balance-application operation are not published
source: TSD P8 v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 (MatchRequest, ProceedsPage, Proceeds); FSD P8 v3 A2.10.2 and A2.10.4.1; Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 (EV-25); context pack P8 ownership rows
description: The legacy criterion needs an answer that says which amount was applied to which part of the balance, and the TSD names MatchRequest and ProceedsPage without a field list and Proceeds without an applied-amount element. No source publishes the operation name of the rwb-case answer that records an amount on the case balance, and the ProceedsMatched payload beyond the general description of slide 43 is not published either. The contract baseline therefore derives the elements from DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009, the query parameters of API-P8-001, the wording of the criterion and the published CloudEvents envelope, marks every field the sources do not give with the placeholder, and holds the consumed rwb-case answer as a consumed and faked row.
evidence: TSD P8 v2 T-A.1 lists only API-P8-001 and API-P8-002, both provided, and T-A.2 names MatchRequest and ProceedsPage without fields; FSD P8 v3 A2.10.4.1 AC-P8-010-01 is one line and A2.10.2 gives no answer shape; Architecture v5 slide 43 row 25 describes ProceedsMatched without a field list; the context pack lists the two P8 provided operations and no consumed one.
owner_role: P8 solution architect and the rwb-case contract owner
proposed: Publish the applied-amount element of the Proceeds answer, the MatchRequest and ProceedsPage field lists and the ProceedsMatched payload in the API Specification and the Service Contract Catalog, and publish the rwb-case balance-application operation and its answer; the baseline then replaces the placeholders and keeps its compatibility rule.
